A_general.open_code_note: No official public repository or package was found in the evidence folder. Hosted endpoint behavior could not be compared with public code.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Splice says searching and building stacks are free for account holders. Downloading requires a Sounds+, Creator, or Creator+ subscription and uses credits; a new sample download costs 1 credit and re-downloads are free. A rolling 24-hour limit of 100 downloads is documented.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The pricing page advertises Splice subscriptions from $4.99; the MCP support page names Sounds+, Creator, and Creator+ as download-eligible plans. Exact current prices for each eligible plan were not fully established from the captured page.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Downloads spend subscription credits; the support page states 1 credit per new sample and free re-downloads. The vendor documents a maximum of 100 sample downloads per rolling 24-hour period. Search and stack creation are free.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: A Splice account and OAuth login are required. Downloading requires a Sounds+, Creator, or Creator+ subscription. The server is described as beta. Shared stack links are public. Splice says ChatGPT is not supported at this time.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor for account access, subscription eligibility, OAuth, and download caps; user controls whether to invoke actions and share a stack.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The endpoint is OAuth-protected. The official support article describes searching, creating and editing stacks, sharing stacks, and downloading samples. Anthropic’s connector directory lists five names: describe_a_sound, create_stack, prompt_to_stack, share_stack, and download_asset. The vendor does not publish tool schemas in the captured official docs.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool result schemas and error formats are NOT FOUND. Official docs describe returned matching samples, downloads, saved stacks, and public share links without specifying MCP result structures.

No MCP-specific logging or audit behavior was found in the reviewed official documentation.

A request to the endpoint returned HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=https://mcp.splice.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`. The protected-resource document reports resource `https://mcp.splice.com/mcp`, authorization server `https://mcp.splice.com`, and scopes `openid`, `profile`, `email`, `offline_access`. The authorization-server metadata reports authorization-code and refresh-token grants, code response type, PKCE S256, token authentication methods `none` and `client_secret_post`, and a registration endpoint. The path-suffixed protected-resource URL and OpenID configuration returned 404. Token lifetime and revocation details were not found.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: OAuth bearer authorization is required; unauthenticated endpoint response was HTTP 401.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration at https://mcp.splice.com/oauth/register; authorization_code and refresh_token grants; PKCE S256; token endpoint auth methods none and client_secret_post; scopes_supported: openid, profile, email, offline_access. Protected resource: https://mcp.splice.com/mcp. Token lifetime and revocation: NOT FOUND.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official docs describe search, stack creation/editing, sharing, and downloads. No tool annotations or schemas were published in the official pages reviewed; the third-party directory names five tools. 2. No server-enforced confirmation, preview approval, or elicitation flow documented. 3. OAuth metadata lists only identity scopes openid, profile, email, offline_access; docs require a Splice account and browser login. Inheritance of product roles, admin switches, client allowlists, redirect URI approval, token lifetime, and revocation are Unknown. 4. The support page gives one global endpoint; no read-only mode, tool filters, sandbox endpoint, or region-specific endpoint found. 5. Official pages state shared links are public. No MCP-specific masking or field boundary documented. Terms prohibit using Sounds as source or training material for AI models. 6. New sample download costs 1 credit; re-downloads are free; limit is 100 samples per rolling 24 hours. 7. Parameter validation, coercion, unknown-argument handling, and overrides are Unknown. 8. MCP-specific logging, audit trails, telemetry, and opt-out are Unknown. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or report tool appears in the listed five names. No MCP upsell result was documented; download eligibility and credit use are explained in docs. 10. No server-delivered skill or initialize instructions found. Docs provide user workflows and examples; enforcement of those recommendations is Unknown. 11. Persistent product state includes stacks saved to the user's library and shared links; whether past agent behavior changes future outputs or tool availability is Unknown. 12. No documented sub-server hierarchy or proxy architecture; a public stack link is a product feature. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or other general escape-hatch tool appears in the five listed names.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The available evidence describes one global hosted MCP endpoint and a flat list of five tools from Anthropic’s directory. The official pages do not publish server architecture details.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official tool-name list or schemas were found in the vendor pages reviewed. MCP.so and MCPBundles could not retrieve tools anonymously because authentication is required. Manufact also reports five tools.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim initialize/tool definitions were available; the endpoint requires OAuth and unauthenticated access returned HTTP 401.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The support article describes editing stacks by renaming, changing BPM, adding/removing layers, and swapping sounds. The five third-party-listed tool names do not establish whether these are separate MCP tools or parameters of other tools. The product's full user interface includes broader catalog browsing, listening/previewing, subscription and credit management, and desktop-app workflows; the MCP docs do not document corresponding MCP actions. The vendor says most AI tools do not play audio inline and sample links must be opened in a browser to preview.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The support article gives example natural-language workflows, including asking to build a beat, refine a stack, find a loop, and download a result. It advises searching specifically for loops when creating a stack from a sample. These are user/client recommendations; no public code or server schema was available to establish enforcement.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The vendor states that shared stack links are public and can be opened by anyone. The support page says new downloads cost one credit, re-downloads are free, and downloads are capped at 100 per rolling 24-hour period. Terms state that Sounds may not be used as source or training material for generative or other AI models.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The product page and support article say searching and building stacks are free; downloading requires a paid plan and credits. The support page says sessions stay connected unless they expire and stacks are saved to the Splice library.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The download-credit and rolling-limit rules are documented as product constraints, but server-side implementation could not be inspected. Public sharing is described as a product property; the five listed tools include share_stack but no schema or enforcement detail. No public code was found to compare against the documentation.

observations_for_research: OAuth scopes are identity-oriented (openid, profile, email, offline_access) while the documented service supports both free search/stack creation and credit-consuming downloads; the metadata exposes no distinct search-versus-download scopes.
Sharing a stack creates a public link accessible to anyone, according to the support page.

The support article documents stack editing capabilities, while Anthropic’s connector directory lists five tools without schemas; the relationship between editing capabilities and those tool names is not specified.
notes: Reviewed links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ and code/GITHUB_COMMITS.txt. No official repository, package, official tool-reference subpage, or public code was found. The official product page describes capabilities but does not expose a tool list; support docs also omit names and schemas. Anthropic’s connector directory is the source of the five tool names, and is third-party evidence. MCP.so and MCPBundles state that live tool discovery requires authentication. A community repository, https://github.com/dreamrec/LivePilot, was listed as unofficial and was not used as evidence. Pricing page capture exposed a general starting price but not a full current breakdown for the download-eligible plans.
